source.description: Every record indexed as Concord law is a subject here. This manifest never decides what counts as law; check-law-coverage.py derives the subject set from the index and fails on any record the manifest omits.

records.reason: Development authority is process law about who owns planned work and merge evidence. It governs how humans and agents use GitHub, not runtime behaviour, so no executable surface exists to bind. It is declared prose-only rather than left undeclared.
Closed historical evidence. CD-0042 retired the pre-go-live surface path this record scoped, so binding it would assert a rule the repository has deliberately superseded.
This decision removes future migration obligations and changes no runtime behavior.
This decision defines an optional external integration boundary and changes no runtime behavior.

Concord development coordination is process law about which authority owns planning, merge, and session evidence. Like CD-0010, it governs how humans and agents work rather than runtime behaviour, so no executable surface exists to bind. Issue #611 closed with the worktree bootstrap it tracked; the decision is declared prose-only rather than left outstanding.

The ladder is process law about the evidence that promotes a Product's maturity and audience claim. It governs how a Product is matured, not runtime behaviour, so no executable surface exists to bind. It is declared prose-only rather than left undeclared.

adapter/opencode/concord.test.ts#work start refuses when the move route is absent
adapter/opencode/concord.test.ts#work start refuses a move the host rejects
adapter/opencode/concord.test.ts#work start verifies the session directory after the move

records.reason: Navigation material with status published, not law. It states a reading order and names companion documents; it asserts no rule an implementation could satisfy or violate. Link integrity, the one property it does carry, is proved by scripts/check-doc-links.py rather than by a coverage anchor on this record.

evidence.value: adapter/opencode/concord.test.ts#a read answered by a newer core contract is typed as version skew

records.reason: Public predecessor design evidence, explicitly non-authorizing. It records what Concord must prevent and is bound by the mechanisms named in the decisions it informed, not by itself.

Predecessor design evidence, explicitly non-authorizing. The failure mechanisms it distills are bound structurally by the decisions that adopted each prevention; the record itself asserts nothing Concord can execute against.
Shaped proposal with deferred open questions and no acceptance marker in its header. It describes a workflow type Concord has not built, so it claims nothing about current behaviour.
Advisory draft rubric that guides where a capability should live. It prescribes nothing an implementation must satisfy.
Living index of open questions and resolved directions. Each resolved item is owned by the decision or spec that resolved it, which carries its own coverage.
Descriptive companion to the manifest. The manifest schema, its generator, and scripts/check-knowledge-closure.py carry the executable authority it describes.

Descriptive architecture companion with status published and no authority over implementations; the decisions and specs it cites carry their own coverage. Its link integrity is proved by scripts/check-doc-links.py.
Aligned companion to priorities.md, which its header names as canonical for the subject. The decisions it aligns to carry their own coverage.

Predecessor capability snapshot marked non-authorizing in its own header; it establishes no proposition this repository can prove or violate, and refreshes against public sources rather than executable evidence.
Descriptive companion. The authorizing record is docs/floor-readiness.v1.json and scripts/check-floor-readiness.py measures it on every run.

Operational guide with status published. It instructs an operator through installer behavior; the installer itself is proved by scripts/test-installer.py and the release pipeline rather than by a coverage anchor on this record.

Investigation findings about an external market, with status published and no authority over Concord. Its claims are about other products and are explicitly caveated in its own unverified section, so they are not propositions this repository can prove by executable evidence. Where a finding influenced Concord's direction, the decision record that adopted it carries the coverage obligation.

Operational procedure for the delivered importer, not law: the policy it serves carries CD-0082's coverage, and the machinery it records is covered by the predecessor inventory and import tests under #295.
Assessment record rather than a prescription. Its internal consistency is validated on every run by scripts/check-predecessor-coverage.py, and each gap it names is owned by its own issue.

The ranked priority order and the operating envelope govern how a design tradeoff is resolved and which capabilities belong in Concord at all. Both are judgements applied by a reader to a proposed change, not propositions about a running system, so no executable anchor can decide whether a given decision honoured the order. Declared prose-only rather than left unmeasured.
Aligned companion that describes the model the accepted decisions establish. CD-0041 and the PM specs carry the coverage for the behaviour it describes.

Constitutional origin record. It names what the public bootstrap excluded and when authority transferred. A running system cannot falsify a historical exclusion, so it is declared prose-only rather than left unmeasured.
Sequencing companion whose header names priorities.md as owner of the ranked priorities. The decisions it sequences carry their own coverage.
Aligned companion describing surfaces the accepted specs establish. It prescribes nothing an implementation must satisfy on its own authority.
Explanatory companion. Its own header states the accepted decisions are binding and this document explains them, so those decisions carry the coverage.
Implementation-acceptance slice whose header states it is ready for acceptance rather than accepted. The PM specs it exercises each carry their own coverage.
Investigation findings on adjacent tooling. It reports options and tradeoffs and reaches no accepted position, so it claims nothing about this Product's behaviour.
Aligned companion to the workflow engine contract, which is the accepted spec and carries the coverage for engine behaviour.
